name: Zipline
readme_summary: Zipline is a Go-based download manager for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It enhances download speeds through multi-connection downloads, supports various file types including torrents and video streams, and offers features like download resuming, scheduling, and bandwidth management.
key_features: Multi-connection downloads (up to 32 per file)
Resumable downloads across restarts and reboots
HLS/DASH stream downloading and conversion to MP4/WebM/MKV
Built-in torrent support (DHT, uTP, port mapping, etc.)
Support for cloud share links (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, etc.)
Browser extension integration (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox)
Download queues, scheduling, and automatic retries
Traffic shaping, quotas, and metered connection management
Private and secure (no accounts, ads, or telemetry)
primary_use_case: Accelerating and managing file downloads from various sources, including direct links, torrents, video streams, and cloud storage.
cover_image_prompt: A vibrant, stylized illustration of a multi-lane highway where each lane is a separate, fast-flowing stream of data (represented by glowing blue particles). A single, sleek vehicle labeled 'Zipline' is effortlessly merging and navigating all these streams simultaneously, collecting them into a single, organized package. In the background, a stylized cityscape with subtle digital elements and progress bars indicates efficient delivery. The overall mood is dynamic and efficient, showcasing the power of parallel processing for downloads. The art style is a clean, modern 3D isometric illustration with a bright, optimistic color palette.

name: cl2metal
description: GPU-rendered terminal + SSH client with a modal editor and a consent-gated MCP agent broker
readme_summary: cl2metal is a GPU-accelerated terminal and SSH client built in Rust. It features a modal editor, advanced terminal capabilities like panes and tabs, robust SSH support including config import and forwards, and integrates a consent-gated MCP agent broker for secure access by local coding agents.
key_features: GPU-rendered terminal with advanced features (OSC 8/52, Kitty protocol, shell integration, panes, tabs)
Comprehensive SSH client (auth methods, jump hosts, forwards, config import, SFTP, remote file editing)
Vim-style modal editor with multiple cursors, splits, file tree, syntax highlighting, find/replace
Consent-gated MCP agent broker for secure access by AI coding agents
Automatic release checking and update prompts
Cross-platform installation scripts for Linux, macOS, and Windows
primary_use_case: To provide a fast, secure, and feature-rich terminal and SSH client experience with integrated modal editing and secure agent access for developers.
cover_image_prompt: A sleek, futuristic terminal interface seamlessly integrated into a stylized, glowing brain. The brain is connected by subtle, luminous data streams to various remote servers represented as distant, crystalline structures. One stream, highlighted with a consent lock icon, flows towards a small, intelligent-looking robot assistant. The terminal display shows a split view: one side with a scrolling terminal output and the other with a file tree and code editor. The overall mood is secure, intelligent, and efficient, with a color palette of deep blues, purples, and glowing cyan accents. The style is a 3D digital illustration with a focus on clean lines and ethereal lighting, subtly incorporating the 'cl2metal' name within the interface.

name: mercury-agent
description: Soul-driven AI agent with permission-hardened tools, token budgets, and multi-channel access. Runs 24/7 from CLI, Telegram or More.
readme_summary: Mercury Agent is a soul-driven AI agent that runs locally on your machine, offering persistent memory, customizable personalities, and a robust permission system. It allows users to interact with the agent through various channels like CLI, Telegram, and Discord, enabling it to perform tasks such as reading/writing files, running commands, and managing code.
key_features: Soul-driven AI agent with customizable personality
Permission-hardened tools
Token budgets for controlled execution
Multi-channel access (CLI, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal)
Persistent memory stored locally
24/7 operation
File system interaction
Command execution
Git and GitHub integration
Web research capabilities
Scheduling
Mercury Code for pair programming
Mercury Bots for persistent specialist teams
primary_use_case: To provide a persistent, customizable, and secure AI agent that runs locally, assisting users with a wide range of tasks from coding to research and automation, while maintaining user control over its actions and data.
cover_image_prompt: A wise, old owl perched on a stack of books, holding a glowing digital key in its talons. The owl is looking directly at the viewer with intelligent eyes, and around it, faint streams of data flow like gentle currents. In the background, a subtle, stylized representation of a computer terminal screen shows lines of code and a small, friendly AI avatar. The scene is set in a cozy, dimly lit study, suggesting a personal, always-on assistant. The overall mood is one of quiet intelligence and reliability. The image should be in a 3D isometric illustration style with a warm, inviting color palette and soft lighting, emphasizing the agent's persistent and helpful nature.

name: witr
description: Why is this running? Trace any process, port, container, or file back to what started it - CLI + TUI.
readme_summary: witr is a command-line and TUI tool that traces the origin of running processes, ports, containers, and files. It answers the question "Why is this running?" by mapping entities back to their originating PID and detailing their ancestry, context, and dependencies, providing output in human-readable reports or machine-readable JSON.
key_features: Trace process, port, container, or file origins
Answers "Why is this running?"
Provides human-readable reports
Outputs machine-readable JSON for scripts and AI agents
Interactive TUI dashboard
Supports Linux, macOS, Windows, and FreeBSD
Available via multiple package managers
primary_use_case: Troubleshooting and understanding the root cause of running processes, services, and resource usage on a system.
cover_image_prompt: A wise old owl, representing 'witr', perched on a complex network of glowing pipes and wires. The owl is holding a magnifying glass, peering intently at a single, brightly lit pipe that traces back through multiple junctions and control valves, revealing its ultimate source. Small, stylized icons representing processes, containers, and files are subtly integrated into the background network. The scene is set in a dimly lit, futuristic control room, with soft, ethereal light emanating from the traced pipe. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clear visual storytelling and a clean, uncluttered composition.

name: CloakBrowser
description: Stealth Chromium that passes every bot detection test. Drop-in Playwright replacement with source-level fingerprint patches. 50+ tests passed.
readme_summary: CloakBrowser is a stealthy Chromium browser designed to bypass bot detection systems. It functions as a drop-in replacement for Playwright and Puppeteer, offering source-level fingerprint patches to make automated browsers appear as normal users.
key_features: Source-level C++ patches for 87 browser fingerprints (canvas, WebGL, audio, etc.)
humanize=True flag for human-like mouse, keyboard, and scroll patterns
High scores on reCAPTCHA v3 and passes Cloudflare Turnstile, FingerprintJS, BrowserScan
Drop-in replacement for Playwright and Puppeteer with same API
Auto-downloads correct Chromium binary, zero configuration
Supports Python and JavaScript
Works with residential proxies and geo-IP matching
primary_use_case: Bypassing bot detection systems in web scraping and automation tasks.
cover_image_prompt: A digital chameleon seamlessly blending into a crowd of diverse, uniquely identifiable individuals. The chameleon, subtly incorporating the 'CloakBrowser' logo, is actively mimicking the digital fingerprints and behaviors of the people around it, making it indistinguishable. In the background, abstract representations of bot detection systems (like security scanners or watchful eyes) are shown failing to identify the chameleon. The scene is vibrant and dynamic, with a clean, modern aesthetic, using a color palette of blues, greens, and subtle purples to convey stealth and sophistication. The overall style should be a 3D isometric illustration, emphasizing the chameleon's adaptive nature and the repository's ability to make automated browsers invisible to detection.
